notes: Both articles before θεός (s008, s018) stand before determinerless English nouns, so rule 21's determinerless clause leaves them unrepresented and keeps of and to with the noun; τῷ θεῷ → to God is rule 21's own example.

τὴν … λατρείαν ὑμῶν is read under rule 92: the expressed predicate noun carries which is, and the article's determiner slot is already occupied by your, which belongs to the available genitive ὑμῶν under rule 20. Reading which as the article's own under rule 31 remains defensible and the unit note records it.
θυσίαν ζῶσαν is anarthrous, so the supplied a belongs to the noun and rides discontinuously around living (rules 15, 58).
